title: 'Prehistoric pterodactyl' with 12-foot wingspan described in UFO files
excerpt: The mystery of a dark-winged creature filmed near the US-Mexico border has deepened after UFO files revealed reports of a giant 'pterodactyl' soaring over America.
content:
The mystery of a dark-winged creature filmed near the US-Mexico border has deepened after UFO files revealed reports of a giant ‘pterodactyl’ in Utah.

The White House's release in October included a 2010 report describing sightings of a ‘pterodactyl-like’ creature with a 12-foot wingspan near a Utah ranch. 

The unnamed witnesses told investigators that they saw a large bird flying overhead after returning home from playing basketball, describing it as 'similar to a prehistoric pterodactyl.'

Witnesses described the beast as black, with a huge beak and the size of an SUV.

The report states that the bird landed across from the witnesses' home, leading them to flee 'because the bird was big enough to pick them up and carry them away.'

Similar claims have emerged this month near Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, where videos purportedly showing a large, dark-winged creature have spread across social media.

One clip, shared by UFO investigator Jaime Maussan, allegedly captured the figure on a home security camera over the Juárez Valley at night, while another appears to show it flying over the city during daylight.

The footage has sparked speculation about a living pterodactyl, alongside accusations that the clips were created using AI.

The White House's release in October included a 2010 report describing sightings of a ‘pterodactyl-like’ creature with a 12-foot wingspan near a Utah ranch

The bizarre clips appear to show a large, winged creature with a long, narrow skull and a prominent crest extending from the back of its head, sparking claims of a living pterodactyl and accusations that the footage was created using AI

The 2010 report details an investigation into alleged unusual activity at Skinwalker Ranch and surrounding communities near Fort Duchesne, Utah.

Skinwalker Ranch is named after the skin-walker, a shapeshifting witch figure from Navajo legend, combined with accounts of strange creatures and local folklore tied to the private property. 

The pterodactyl sighting was buried among other bizarre accounts in the report, including a dog-like creature with a human-looking nose, towering shadows and unexplained lights. 

Investigators collected the account from a family whose names and identifying details were redacted from the document.

A witness-description table dates one account to the summer of 2006 or 2007, several years before investigators conducted their 2010 field visits.

The witnesses said they could hear the creature’s wings flapping and both saw and heard branches moving as it descended into the trees.

The interview notes estimated its head and beak at two to three feet long, while the accompanying table described it as standing approximately four feet high.

One witness recalled its legs hanging beneath its body during flight, ‘like that of a bird.’ Another described its wings moving in an arc, estimating that a single wing was as long as a car and four feet wide.

The report states that the bird landed across from the witnesses' home, leading them to flee 'because the bird was big enough to pick them up and carry them away'

The interview account ends without an explanation for what they encountered: the pair said they never saw the creature again and did not know where it went afterward.

The 2010 file came just weeks before mysterious sightings of a similar creature emerged along the US-Mexico border. 

The uncertainty about the videos' authenticity has done little to dampen speculation online. 'There was a Pterodactyl in Mexico! Who let the monster out?' one user wrote.

Another posted: 'A pterodactyl shows up in Mexico. Scientists claim it's a bird. Nice try, Jurassic Park. We're not falling for that s***.'

Ciudad Juárez’s municipal Civil Protection director, Sergio Rodríguez, dismissed the prehistoric-animal claims as unsupported, describing the videos as digital entertainment without a factual basis, according to local outlet Radio Net.

The video shows a winged silhouette over the Juárez Valley at night

TV Azteca cited unnamed specialists who suggested the figure could be a great blue heron

Separately, TV Azteca cited unnamed specialists who suggested the figure could be a great blue heron, although the report provided no named expert or detailed analysis supporting that identification.

Maussan has offered his own speculative explanation, asking on X: 'Is the creature recently filmed in the Juárez Valley evidence that a dimensional portal is located there?'

He was suggesting that the figure might have entered our world through a supposed gateway to another dimension, a theory for which he provided no scientific evidence.

In an episode of his program Interestelar, Maussan also revised his identification of the alleged creature, saying that what he had previously described as a pterodactyl was, in his view, a Pteranodon.

'We were mistaken,' he acknowledged, arguing that its apparent size and head crest supported his revised interpretation.

The program presented a third recording, reportedly filmed on November 7 around 11pm local time at the intersection of Margarita and Arroyo de las Víboras streets in the Felipe Ángeles neighborhood.

A narrated report attributed the footage to a boy named Fernando Arteaga, who allegedly witnessed the figure attacking a dog before taking flight.

'According to his account, the strange creature attacked a dog and tried to carry it away, releasing it at the last moment. It then took flight,' the report stated.

A local claimed to have captured the creature soaring over the city earlier this month

The broadcast said the boy began filming as the figure rose into the night sky, turned and disappeared from view. That account has not been independently corroborated.

The report pointed to the Franklin Mountains in nearby El Paso, Texas, as a geographical reference visible in the background.

According to the broadcast, Maussan Television collaborators Eduardo Gamaliel and Marcos Carrera visited the location where the boy said he made the recording.

The program also highlighted a sound it attributed to the flying figure, although its source was not independently established.

Its identification of the alleged creature relied partly on what the team interpreted as a crest extending from the back of its head.

'This characteristic is fundamental to establishing that it is a Pteranodon,' the narrated report stated.

Maussan acknowledged that the images remained under investigation, while also describing the evidence presented on his program as 'absolutely authentic.'
